claims.text: An optimal concentration of X minimizes lattice mismatch between the CrFeCoNiX substrate and the growing Cr-rich oxide.
The relevant protective oxide is Cr-rich and may be Cr2O3.
Minimal substrate/oxide lattice mismatch enables epitaxial, coherent oxide growth.
Epitaxial, coherent oxide growth remains structurally stable above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Deviation from the optimal X concentration increases oxide/substrate misfit strain.
Increased misfit strain promotes oxide cracking and spallation.
Changing the concentration of Si, Mn, or Al adjusts the lattice parameters of the alloy substrate.
An optimized X concentration makes the substrate lattice parameter closely match that of the forming Cr-rich oxide.
A coherent oxide/substrate interface minimizes interfacial stress.
Suboptimal X concentrations generate significant misfit strain and tensile stress at the oxide/substrate interface.
Misfit-generated tensile stress causes oxide cracking and spallation during thermal exposure.
Alloys at the optimal X concentration will form a thin, continuous, coherent protective oxide.
The oxide formed at the optimal X concentration will have low residual interfacial strain and slow growth.
Non-optimal X concentrations will produce greater interfacial misfit and residual stress.
Non-optimal X concentrations will cause premature oxide cracking or spallation.
A baseline alloy with minimal or default X content is expected to show poorer oxide coherence and more pronounced oxide failure than an optimized alloy.
The proposed comparison uses single-phase solid-solution CrFeCoNiX alloys exposed at 900–1000 °C for approximately 100–500 hours under controlled oxidative or mildly corrosive conditions.
Applicability of the mechanism to multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys is not established.
